test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 28 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The problem of myopia in human eye can be corrected by using:

options.text: a convex lens of suitable power
a convex mirror of suitable focal length
a concave lens of suitable power

solution:
The correct answer is __**a concave lens of suitable power**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Myopia, also known as nearsightedness, is a common vision condition where distant objects appear blurry.
 
• This condition occurs when the eyeball is too long or the cornea is too curved, causing light rays to focus in front of the retina.
 
• Myopia can be corrected by using a concave lens, which diverges light rays before they enter the eye, allowing them to focus on the retina.
 
• Concave lenses are specified with a negative diopter value, indicating their ability to correct nearsightedness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hyperopia (Farsightedness)**

 
 
• Hyperopia is a condition where distant objects are seen more clearly than near objects.
 
• This condition occurs when the eyeball is too short or the cornea is not curved enough, causing light to focus behind the retina.
 
• Hyperopia can be corrected by using convex lenses, which converge light rays before they enter the eye.
 
 
 
• **Astigmatism**
 
 
• Astigmatism is a common vision condition that causes blurred vision due to an irregularly shaped cornea or lens.
 
• This irregular shape prevents light from focusing properly on the retina, leading to distorted or blurred vision at all distances.
 
• Astigmatism can be corrected using cylindrical lenses that compensate for the irregular curvature of the cornea or lens.
 
 
 
• **Presbyopia**
 
 
• Presbyopia is an age-related condition where the eye gradually loses the ability to focus on near objects.
 
• This condition typically becomes noticeable in the early to mid-40s and continues to worsen with age.
 
• It can be corrected using reading glasses, bifocals, or progressive lenses.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Errors**
 
 
• Refractive errors occur when the shape of the eye prevents light from focusing directly on the retina.
 
• Common refractive errors include myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism, and presbyopia.
 
• These errors can be corrected with the use of prescription lenses, contact lenses, or refractive surgery.
